content:
Diego: Heads-up — Q1 hosted API capacity planning kickoff. We need a decision on new GPU buys vs short-term leases for the May->July burst window.
Priya: Agree. Our throughput projection for that window is +48% traffic y/y based on monthly trends and a new partner launch. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Ava: Finance prefers a mixed approach. Capex is tight but long-term unit cost favors buys. Need numbers.
Marcus: Technical constraints: EU availability for A100 80GB is 2–3 weeks lead if buying, leasing options are available with 24–72h spin up but higher $/GPU-hour and risk of preemption.
Priya: Quick calc I ran: baseline 150k GPU-hours for Q2 normal, surge adds ~72k hours. If we target 90% on hosted dedicated fleet, we need ~200k committed hours.
capacity-bot: Forecast snapshot uploaded: https://internal/redwood/capacity/1769098765 — includes per-region demand heatmap and cost sims.
Sam: Can we absorb some demand with smarter batching + KV-cache tuning to shave peak token throughput? That could reduce needed GPU-hours by ~15%.
Marcus: Yes, can patch runtime to increase batching time window to 15ms for non-low-latency routes. Risk: small P50 increase for chat endpoints.
Diego: Tradeoff table pls: buy vs lease vs hybrid, include lead time, unit $/hr, failure modes, ops overhead. Priya/Ava can you populate?
Ava: I'll add TCO for 3-year amortization vs 6-month lease in the spreadsheet. Early numbers: buy A100 80GB ~ $?? (we use placeholder until final quote) — effective $/GPU-hour ~0.35 with 24/7 utilization. Lease spotrange ~ $0.85/hr but includes vendor-managed replacements.
Priya: Also factoring regional constraints: APAC capacity limited; suggestion: route APAC burst to eu-west / us-west with region-aware routing and a small latency SLO relaxation for non-interactive tasks.
Marcus: For network egress cost: moving more long-tail batch jobs cross-region will add $12k-20k for the quarter. Add that to TCO.
Diego: Security note: private deployments for enterprise customers can't be placed on burst lease instances unless we vet the vendor. So some revenue bucket requires owned hardware or Dedicated reserved tenant pools.
Sam: Ops overhead: leases require different runbook for node churn and spot-like replacers. We should estimate ~0.5 FTE for lifecycle ops during the Q2 window.
Priya: Putting a proposal: commit to buy 40% of incremental capacity (long-lived), lease 60% for peak. This reduces upfront cost while giving predictable base capacity.
Ava: That aligns with finance risk appetite. Need final quotes and a small capital approval for the buy tranche.
Marcus: Can we prototype the runtime batching tweak in canary next week and measure latency P50/P95? If we get ~10–15% token cost reduction, we can shrink the lease portion.
Diego: Action items: Priya — update spreadsheet with region breakouts + burst-days calc by EOD Thu. Ava — get vendor buy quotes and 6-month lease pricing by Fri. Marcus — run canary for batching and KV-cache adjustments by Tue. Sam — draft runbook for lease node churn.
Priya: Noted. Also scheduling a 30m sync on Monday to decide commit levels before procurement.
Diego: Perfect. If anyone has blockers ping me directly. :+1:
capacity-bot: Reminder: procurement approval cutoff for Q2 orders is 1769185165 (one week).
Marcus: One more thought — add a fallback policy to route to smaller quantized models under extreme pressure to protect SLA. Will draft config.
Ava: Good idea — include cost delta for fallback and expected quality delta.
Sam: I'll cold-start the runbook template and link it in the spreadsheet.
Diego: Thanks team — will summarize outcome after Monday sync.
